observations: Photos 0 to 2: one foot-mounted cycloidal gear reducer (speed reducer) with a large round motor-input flange on one end and a keyed output shaft under a yellow protective cap on the other.
Cast iron body with ribbed housing rings, a lifting eye, and two plugs on top (breather and oil fill).
The whole unit is freshly painted bright blue, including bolt heads, so it is a refurbished used unit, not new.
No nameplate, brand, ratio or power rating is visible in any photo.
No motor is attached; photos are taken on a tiled floor with a dealer watermark; no scale reference.

identity.kind: cycloidal gear reducer, foot mounted, cast body
read_from: photo 0 housing shape and output shaft
photo 1 side view with foot and input flange

claims.evidence: Photos 0 to 2 show a cycloidal speed reducer.
No nameplate or rating plate is shown; the size cannot be measured without a scale reference.
Photos 0 to 2 show a cast housing and cast foot.

risks.risk: Power rating and ratio may be lower than claimed
risks.proof: Close photo of the nameplate showing model, ratio and kW or hp, or a photo of the shaft and flange with a tape measure across them
risks.if_unproven: as the smallest size consistent with the photos, below the claimed range

risks.risk: Fresh paint may hide cracks, welds or a rebuilt housing; internal pins and bearings may be worn
risks.proof: Clip of the reducer running under a motor, or the output shaft turned by hand showing no play, with a handwritten code in shot
Close photo of the input and output seals after a run

proof_requests: Close photo of the nameplate with ratio and rating, or a tape measure across the shaft and flange
Clip of it running under a motor with a handwritten code in shot
Close photos of the seals and the underside
response.reason: The photos plainly show a refurbished cycloidal gear reducer, a plain industrial good priced by type, so it is priced at its worst case as untested and at the low end of its size until the nameplate or a running clip is shown.
